Every month, our technology powers tens of millions of dollars in donations across the globe. We focus on innovation that directly impacts results: faster load times, higher conversion rates, global payment support, and accessibility-first design. Our platform is trusted by many of the world’s leading nonprofits, including UNICEF, the Alzheimer’s Association, and a wide range of global NGOs. With a 4.9/5 rating across top software review platforms, we’re recognized not just for our impact - but for the quality of the product we deliver. A Truly Global Product We operate in the enterprise segment, serving nonprofit organizations across North America, the United Kingdom, Australia, and Europe. We’re building a large and complex product ecosystem that serves nonprofits, donors, and partners around the world. The platform includes a modern checkout experience and customizable widgets (each a standalone SPA), donor, organization, and partner portals , admin tools , and several internal apps. The Team We are a distributed team of 160+ product professionals. Our team members are mainly based across Spain, Poland, Portugal, Georgia, Armenia, Serbia, Turkey, and Cyprus. Despite our scale, we operate like a focused team - where every task matters and every voice is heard. We value thoughtful collaboration, strong engineering practices, and a product mindset. You’ll be joining a team where quality, mentorship, and mutual respect come first. About In-Person Giving At Fundraise Up In-Person Giving brings the quality and connected data of Fundraise Up’s online donation experience into physical fundraising moments. The product begins with Tap to Donate and Giving Station: staff-led and self-service experiences that let nonprofits accept contactless donations at events, in public spaces, and through other offline workflows. Every transaction should connect to the same campaigns, donor records, reporting, CRM integrations, and operational controls used across Fundraise Up. The next product direction is Events & Commerce . It includes ticket sales, check-in, merchandise and food purchases, symbolic purchases, auctions, paddle raises, and additional donations before and during an event. These capabilities must work as one connected fundraising system rather than another isolated event tool. About The Role We are hiring a Product Manager to own Events & Commerce within the broader In-Person Giving product line. This is a hands-on software product role covering discovery, definition, delivery, launch, and iteration. You will turn a large category into a focused product direction grounded in customer workflows, live usage, and commercial evidence. You will work closely with the PM responsible for the broader In-Person Giving area so that event commerce builds on the same payment, campaign, donor-data, reporting, mobile, and operational foundations as Tap to Donate and Giving Station. You will also partner with the Peer-to-Peer team where ticketing and event capabilities should be shared rather than rebuilt separately. This is not an event-planning, sales, or internal project-coordination role. What You’ll Own Define the product direction Turn customer research, market evidence, and business context into a clear Events & Commerce product thesis and sequenced roadmap. Choose a focused target segment and event scenario rather than trying to replace every event platform at once. Decide which capabilities belong in the shared In-Person Giving foundation and which require an Events-specific model. Make explicit decisions about what Fundraise Up should build, integrate, partner on, or deliberately exclude. Keep assumptions, success metrics, scope, risks, and product decisions visible. Lead discovery and product definition Work directly with nonprofit fundraising teams, event operators, finance teams, volunteers, attendees, donors, design partners, and internal GTM teams. Map the complete workflow before, during, and after an event—including purchase, donation, check-in, fulfillment, reconciliation, reporting, and follow-up. Validate decisions through interviews, workflow observation, prototypes, and live product usage. Separate true adoption blockers from feature requests and expectations created by incumbent event platforms. Shape problems such as ticket sales, QR-based check-in, guest management, commerce catalogues, FMV and receipts, on-site purchases, auctions, paddle raises, refunds, attribution, reporting, and integrations. These are examples—not a pre-committed feature checklist. Shape and deliver the product Own the product from problem definition through requirements, delivery, launch, and iteration. Write clear requirements, acceptance criteria, edge cases, state transitions, and decision records. Make day-to-day scope and trade-off decisions with Engineering, Design, Analytics, Research, QA, and GTM partners. Design for real event conditions: staff and volunteer operators, self-service flows, mobile devices, optional hardware, unreliable connectivity, high-volume moments, and operational recovery. Ensure that event capabilities reuse Fundraise Up’s existing payments, campaign, donor, reporting, CRM, and identity infrastructure wherever possible. Keep delivery predictable by surfacing dependencies, risks, and unresolved decisions early. Launch, learn, and drive outcomes Launch through EAPs with clear entry criteria, target workflows, success measures, readiness requirements, and out-of-scope areas. Understand whether organizations can configure and run the target event workflows without heavy manual work or disconnected tools. Measure whether attendees can purchase, check in, donate, and receive the right confirmation or receipt through a clear experience. Partner with Product Marketing, Sales, CSM, Support, Finance, Legal, and Operations on positioning, commitments, enablement, and launch readiness. Connect product evidence to activation, adoption, event completion, GPV, expansion, pipeline, retention, and operational cost. Turn evidence into explicit recommendations: iterate, expand, change direction, partner, or stop. Work AI-native Use AI for research synthesis, workflow analysis, prototyping, specification quality, data exploration, and operational automation. Build testable artifacts quickly without outsourcing product judgment. Requirements 4–7 years of Product Management or Product Ownership experience in a software product company. End-to-end ownership of a customer-facing product area with Engineering and Design. Strong judgment in reducing a large problem space to a focused release and explaining the trade-offs. Experience turning customer evidence and product data into decisions. Clear written communication across requirements, edge cases, metrics, and decision records. Ability to work with transactional, multi-actor workflows involving permissions, states, money, and data relationships. High ownership and independence, with fluent written and spoken English. Strong plus Experience with ticketing, event technology, commerce, POS, payments, marketplaces, registration, auctions, or other transaction-heavy products. Experience with mobile applications, contactless payments, physical devices, or hardware-enabled workflows. Experience with B2B SaaS, fundraising, nonprofits, or other operationally complex customer environments. Experience launching a new product area through beta or EAP. Knowledge of CRM integrations, financial reconciliation, reporting, transaction attribution, analytics, or SQL. Practical use of AI for research, prototyping, analysis, or product operations. This Role May Not Be a Fit If You are looking for an event-planning or internal project-management role rather than software product ownership. You prefer to receive a fully defined roadmap and requirements instead of helping determine what should be built. You want to work only on strategy and avoid specifications, QA, delivery details, or post-launch iteration. You treat every customer request as a roadmap commitment. You need stable scope and certainty before moving forward. You measure progress mainly by features shipped rather than customer and business outcomes. Why work with us Build a new product direction from research through live customer use. Work in a large, proven fundraising category with clear customer demand and meaningful commercial potential. Shape ticketing and event commerce as part of a broader fundraising platform rather than an isolated event tool. Work with real nonprofit customers, rich product evidence, and experienced cross-functional partners. Join a small team where product managers have meaningful ownership and direct access to Product leadership. Help define an AI-native approach to product management in practice. review_candidates.title: International Account Manager Europa
review_candidates.description: Voor Damaco foods zoeken we een International Account Manager voor de Europese markt. Als International Account Manager ben je verantwoordelijk voor het onderhouden en verder uitbouwen van de bestaande klantenportefeuille in Europa. Samen met het team bouw je mee aan die relaties en zorgt ervoor dat de bestaande business verder groeit. Functie-omschrijving: Als International Sales Manager ben je verantwoordelijk voor het beheren en ontwikkelen van onze exportmarkten in Europa. Je speelt een sleutelrol in onze internationale activiteiten door sterke klantrelaties op te bouwen en ook nieuwe commerciële kansen te identificeren. Concreet: - Het onderhouden en versterken van relaties met bestaande klanten en tegelijkertijd actief op zoek gaan naar nieuwe zakelijke kansen. - Het opbouwen en onderhouden van langdurige partnerschappen met klanten en zakenpartners. - Het monitoren van marktontwikkelingen en proactief inspelen op veranderende klantbehoeften. - Het vertegenwoordigen van het bedrijf tijdens internationale zakenreizen. - Deelname aan internationale beurzen en branche-evenementen waar we regelmatig aanwezig is, zoals Anuga, SIAL, Gulfood en andere toonaangevende branchebeurzen. Functie-eisen: - Je hebt minimaal 2-5 jaar ervaring in internationale verkoop. - Je hebt voeling met de voeding. - Je beschikt over een sterke commerciële instelling en vindt het leuk om nieuwe zakelijke kansen te ontwikkelen en langdurige klantrelaties te onderhouden. - Je bent proactief, ondernemend en kunt zelfstandig werken. - Je bent leergierig en kunt zich aanpassen aan verschillende regionale bedrijfsculturen en -wijzen. - Je brengt van nature enthousiasme, energie en een positieve houding mee naar het team. - Je bent dus een team-player. - Vloeiende beheersing van het Nederlands, Frans en Engels is essentieel vanwege het internationale karakter van de functie. Kennis van het Duits en/of Spaans is een pluspunt. Aanbod: Een boeiende en zelfstandige functie binnen een ambitieuze en internationaal georiënteerde organisatie. - De kans om bij te dragen aan de verdere internationale groei van ons bedrijf. een bedrijf die meer dan een gevestigde waarde is en meer dan 50 jaar bestaat. - Een aantrekkelijk salaris, inclusief: o Een prestatiebonus o Bedrijfswagen o Groepsverzekering o Ziekenhuisverzekering o 6 extra vakantiedagen (ADV-dagen)
